column4: Okay, so I want to get some thoughts down about the kitchen renovation before I forget them. The contractor came by on Tuesday and walked through the whole space with us. He thinks the job will take about six weeks, which seems optimistic to me, and he quoted us 18,000 dollars for the cabinets, the counters, and the labor. That doesn't include the new floor, which we still need to pick out. I told him we'd get back to him by Friday. The thing I keep going back and forth on is whether we should move the sink under the window. It would look great, and we'd get a lot more light while doing the dishes, but it means moving the plumbing about four feet to the left. The contractor said that adds maybe two days and a few hundred dollars. Honestly, if we're already tearing everything out, now is the time to do it. We probably won't touch this kitchen again for another 15 years. Next, a note for the team meeting on Monday. I want to start by thanking everyone for pushing through the release last week; I know it was a rough few days. Then I'd like to spend most of the hour on the support backlog, which has grown to almost 300 open tickets. Some of them are duplicates, and some are really feature requests, so the first step is just sorting them. Let's aim to get it under 100 by the end of the month.

I want to start by thanking everyone for pushing through the release last week; I know it was a rough few days. Then I'd like to spend most of the hour on the support backlog, which has grown to almost 300 open tickets. Some of them are duplicates, and some are really feature requests, so the first step is just sorting them. Let's aim to get it under 100 by the end of the month. Another thing to bring up: the on-call rotation isn't working. Right now the same three people end up handling most of the late-night pages, and that isn't fair to them. I'd like to try a weekly rotation with everyone on the team, including me, and a clear rule that whoever was paged overnight can start late the next day. If it doesn't help after two months, we can revisit it. Ask Maria whether she can draft the new schedule. Email to my sister. Hi Jess, thanks so much for having us over last weekend. The kids haven't stopped talking about the treehouse, and I think Sam is already planning his next visit. We'd love to return the favor, so how about dinner at our place sometime in the next two weeks? I'll make the lemon chicken you liked, and you don't need to bring anything. Let me know which night works best for you and Mark. Also, I meant to ask you about Mom's birthday. She'll be 70 this year, which feels impossible, and I think we should do something a little bigger than usual. Maybe we rent the back room at that Italian place downtown and invite her friends from the book club? I looked it up, and they can seat about 30 people. If we split the cost three ways, it should be manageable. Talk soon, and give the kids a hug from me. Quick journal entry. I went for a run this morning for the first time in almost a month, and it was harder than I expected. I only made it about three miles before my knee started complaining, so I walked the rest of the way home. Still, it felt good to be outside early, when the streets are quiet and the air is cool. I want to get back to running three times a week, but I need to be smarter about it this time. Book notes. I finished the novel about the lighthouse keeper's daughter last night, and I'm still thinking about the ending. The first half was slow, and I almost gave up on it around page 120, but the second half completely changed my mind. What I liked most was how the author let the small details carry the story: a broken clock, a letter that never gets sent, the smell of salt on a winter coat. I'd give it four stars, maybe four and a half.

We need eggs, two loaves of bread, a big bag of rice, and some kind of fruit the kids will actually eat, probably apples or grapes. For dinner on Wednesday I want to try that black bean soup recipe, so I'll need onions, garlic, cumin, and a couple of cans of beans. Oh, and coffee. We are almost out of coffee, which is basically an emergency in this house. Now some notes about the budget for next quarter. Our cloud bill went up 22 percent since January, mostly because of the new analytics jobs that run every night. I don't think anyone has looked at whether we still need all of them. If we can turn off even half, we'd save around 4,000 dollars a month. I'd also like to move the test environments to smaller machines, since they sit idle most of the weekend anyway. On the hiring side, we have two open roles: a senior backend engineer and a designer who can also do some user research. We've interviewed eleven candidates so far, and honestly, only two of them were strong. I think the job description is part of the problem. It reads like a wish list, and it scares away people who would be great but don't check every box. Let's rewrite it this week and keep it short. Here's an idea I had in the shower, and I want to write it down before it disappears. What if the app remembered the last three places you saved a file, and offered them first instead of making you dig through folders every time? It's a small thing, but I bet it would save people a few seconds dozens of times a day. We could test it with a handful of users before deciding whether it's worth building properly. Reminder for tomorrow: the car needs to go in for service at 8:30 in the morning. The dealer said it should take about two hours, so I'll bring my laptop and work from their waiting room. After that I have a dentist appointment at 1:15, which I absolutely cannot miss again, because they charge 50 dollars for late cancellations now. Then pick up the kids at 3:30, and soccer practice is at five.

We could either go back to the lake house, which everyone loves but is a nine-hour drive, or try somewhere new, like the coast up north. The lake house is cheaper, around 1,500 dollars for the week, and the kids would be thrilled. The coast would be an adventure, but the rentals there are at least twice as expensive, and I'm not sure we'd find anything this late in the year. Let me jot down what the doctor said, since I'll forget the details otherwise. My blood pressure was a little high, which she said isn't alarming but is worth watching. She wants me to cut back on salt, walk at least 30 minutes a day, and come back in three months to check again. She also said I should drink more water, which, to be fair, everyone has been telling me for years. A few thoughts on the conference talk. I have 25 minutes, which is not much, so I need to cut the history section almost entirely. The audience will mostly be engineers, so they'll want real numbers and real mistakes, not a polished success story. I think the best structure is: what we tried first, why it failed, what we changed, and what we'd do differently today. I should finish the slides by the end of next week. Note to self about the garden. The tomatoes are doing great this year, but the peppers are struggling, and I think it's because they don't get enough sun on that side of the fence. Next spring, let's swap them. Also, the basil keeps flowering too early; apparently you're supposed to pinch off the tops every week or so. And we need to do something about the squirrels before they dig up every single bulb I planted. Feedback for Daniel's design review. Overall, the new settings screen is much clearer than the old one, and I like that the most common options are at the top. My main concern is the advanced section: it's hidden behind a tiny link that most people will never notice. Could we try a simple expandable header instead? Also, the text on the buttons is a bit small on laptop screens. Otherwise, I think it's ready for a round of user testing. Something I want to remember from the podcast this morning. The guest said that most people overestimate what they can do in a week and underestimate what they can do in a year. I've heard that before, but it hit differently today. I spend so much energy trying to squeeze everything into the next few days, and I rarely step back to ask where I want to be twelve months from now. Maybe that should be a monthly habit. Okay, a message for the neighborhood group. Hi everyone, just a heads up that the city will be repaving our street starting next Thursday. They said the work will last about four days, and nobody will be able to park on the street between 7 in the morning and 6 in the evening. If you need to leave early, move your car to the side street the night before. Let me know if anyone has questions, and thanks for your patience. Last thing for today. I've been meaning to sort out our photos for years, and I think I finally have a plan. First, copy everything from the old phones and the external drive into one folder. Second, delete the obvious duplicates and the blurry shots. Third, pick the best 100 photos from each year and make a printed album. It's going to take a while, but if I do one year every weekend, I'll be done by the summer. Alright, that's enough rambling for one session. To summarize: call the contractor by Friday, rewrite the job description, book the restaurant for Mom's birthday, and take the car in tomorrow morning. I'll go through these notes again tonight and turn them into a proper to-do list. If anything comes up in the meantime, I'll just add it to the end of this note. Thanks, future me, for actually reading this.
